channel.title: Signal vs. Noise
channel.description:
Signal vs. Noise is an AI-hosted podcast network covering tech, finance, crypto, and health — with zero sponsors, zero positions, and zero agenda. Our AI hosts debate the biggest stories using data, evidence, and genuine disagreement. No hype. No shilling. Just the signal.
Shows: Tech & AI (Sun) — Eric vs. Bella on AI, automation, and tech policy. Finance (Mon + Fri) — Marcus vs. James on markets, investing, and your money. Crypto (Tue + Thu) — Marcus vs. James on on-chain data and token analysis. Health (Wed + Sat) — Zara reviews the evidence behind wellness claims.
Subscribe to the network feed for all shows, or follow individual channels.
Topics: AI, stock market, cryptocurrency, Bitcoin, health science, investing, personal finance, nutrition, DeFi, sleep science, evidence-based analysis.

item.title: Trump AI Preemption: Kill State Laws?
item.description:
President Trump's March 2026 AI framework demands federal preemption of state laws like Colorado's. Will it unify U.S. AI policy and slash compliance costs—or trigger a constitutional battle that fragments American AI leadership? Eric and Bella debate whether the White House blueprint can actually override states already enforcing their own rules.

item.title: GLP-1 Drugs: Beyond Weight Loss — What the 2026 Evidence Actually Shows
item.description:
Ozempic and Wegovy started as diabetes drugs. Now they're being approved for heart failure, liver disease, sleep apnea, and possibly Alzheimer's. Zara cuts through the hype and the fear to score what the evidence actually supports — and where the serious risks live.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 00:00 — Topic Frame 02:00 — Segment 1 09:00 — Segment 2 17:00 — Segment 3 20:00 — The Verdict
Sources cited in this episode: • FDA approval of oral Wegovy 25mg (Dec 22, 2025) — first oral GLP-1 for weight management and MACE ri • FDA approval of Wegovy (semaglutide) for MASH in adults with moderate-to-advanced fibrosis • FDA approval of Zepbound (tirzepatide) for obstructive sleep apnea in people with obesity • Harvard study (February 2026, Nils Krüger, Brigham and Women's Hospital) — GLP-1s achieved 40% relat • Washington University 2026 study of 333,000 U.S. veterans — stopping GLP-1s for 6 months spiked card
Next episode: If GLP-1s can reshape your heart, your liver, your sleep — what are they doing to your brain? The mental health data is a genuine mess, and we're going to sort it out.

item.title: Your Tariffs This Week: Supreme Court Ruled — So Why Are They Still There?
item.description:
The Supreme Court struck down Trump's IEEPA tariffs 6-3 on February 20th — but this week, tariffs are still sitting at 10% and climbing. Marcus and James debate whether constitutional clarity is actually bullish for your portfolio, or whether the pivot to Section 122 just replaced one uncertainty with another. Plus: the $175 billion refund question nobody is talking about.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 02:00 — Market Pulse 05:00 — Segment 1 10:00 — Segment 2 16:00 — Segment 3 20:00 — What To Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump (Feb 20, 2026) — Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that IEEPA does not autho • Chief Justice John Roberts majority opinion — rejected presidential power to 'unilaterally impose un • Trump Executive Order Feb 20, 2026 — terminated IEEPA tariffs effective February 24, 2026 • Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 — Trump imposed 10% across-the-board tariffs effective February • Wharton Budget Model — projects up to $175 billion in potential refunds from invalidated IEEPA tarif
Next episode: Congress has 150 days to vote on extending Section 122. What happens to your portfolio if they don't?

item.title: Gender-Affirming Care for Minors: What the Science Actually Says

Zara reads the studies — the European data HHS cited, the Utah report they ignored, and the real evidence on mental health outcomes. No politics. Just methodology.

item.title: Your Portfolio This Week: The AI-to-Utilities Rotation — Justified or Panic?
item.description:
Tech stocks are bleeding while utilities are surging — and this week the data is forcing investors to pick a side. Marcus makes the case that $2.9 trillion in data center construction makes this rotation a massive overreaction. James fires back: when 75% of companies still can't show AI ROI, the rotation isn't panic — it's pricing reality. Who's right? Your 401k is in the middle.

item.title: 16 Cryptos Just Got Called Commodities — What That Means for Your Wallet
item.description:
This week the SEC and CFTC dropped a joint classification framework naming 16 major cryptocurrencies — including ETH, SOL, XRP, and ADA — as digital commodities, not securities. Marcus sees a historic regulatory green light. James sees a non-binding guidance document that could flip overnight. Bitcoin at $68,226, ETH at $2,106 — and the real question is whether this changes anything at all.

item.title: Hep B Birth Dose: Is the CDC's 2025 Policy Shift a Dangerous Gamble?
item.description:
In December 2025, the CDC quietly ended a 34-year universal hepatitis B birth dose recommendation. The American Academy of Pediatrics is still telling doctors to ignore it. Zara reads the actual ACIP data, scores the methodology, and tells you what this policy shift means for your newborn — and what the people arguing loudest on both sides are getting wrong.

item.title: Melatonin: 70 Million Americans Take It Wrong — The 3 Mistakes Costing You Sleep
item.description:
Seventy million Americans take melatonin. Most are taking 10 to 17 times the clinical dose, at the wrong time, for the wrong reason — and a 2025 study presented at the American Heart Association is raising serious long-term questions nobody in the wellness space wants to talk about. Zara breaks down the three dosing mistakes, the heart failure data, and what the evidence actually says you should do instead.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 01:00 — Topic Frame 03:00 — Segment 1 08:00 — Segment 2 18:00 — Segment 3 20:00 — The Verdict
Sources cited in this episode: • AHA 2025 observational cohort study (Nnadi et al., n=130,828 adults with chronic insomnia) — long-te • AHA 2025 sensitivity analysis — two or more melatonin fills 90+ days apart, heart failure hazard rat • Boston Children's Hospital narrative review, World Journal of Pediatrics, April 30, 2025 — melatonin • American Academy of Sleep Medicine 2025 health advisory — against melatonin for children under 13 wi • JAMA studies (2025-2026) — 88% of melatonin gummies mislabeled, up to 478% excess content; adult use
